In instances where a pay plan is in use by an organization, the COLA increases that pay plan by a specified percentage while also increasing each eligible employee’s pay by that same percentage.
To be eligible for the entire COLA amount an employee must simply be at the maximum of the pay plan or less.
Employees who are at the maximum will remain at the maximum as the pay plan is increased by the same percentage as the employees’ salaries are increased.
Employees whose pay exceeds the current maximum of their range by more than the COLA percentage would not receive an adjustment in pay.
I have developed a preliminary recommended pay plan.
In so doing, by identifying employees through the use of unofficial data who would receive a pay increase, you are no longer discussing a COLA.

The Member will continue to receive all specialty, education, longevity, acting and other pays the Member is entitled to for the duration of the assignment. 46 SECTION 24.

Policy 7.5.A: Funding for Quality of Life Services Synopsis: Continue to identify and provide funding for services and amenities that contribute to quality of life and economic vitality of the community, including parks and recreation, cultural and library facilities, and other services. 2.

Even though the projects recommended for impact fee funding are selected from the long-­‐ range Transportation Master Plan, the “need” for transportation improvements is more difficult to determine for streets than for utility systems.
Conversely, if elected officials desire to expand the list of transportation improvements, proposed impact fees would increase proportionately.
If Cheyenne’s elected officials make a legislative policy decision to not impose fees by house size, TischlerBise will recommend that fees be imposed for two residential categories.
The reorganized authority shall consist of newly appointed board members numbering not less than five nor more than eleven (11) members appointed by the governing body.
The affairs of the authority shall be under the direct supervision and control of a the board consisting of ten (10) members appointed by the mayor with the advice and consent of the governing body.
At least one member shall be a member of the governing body appointed to serve at the pleasure of the governing body; 2.
Nine members shall be appointed by the mayor in accordance with the by-law of the downtown development authority.
The remaining members shall be appointed to staggered terms in accordance with Wyo.
A member shall hold office until his or her successor has been appointed and qualified.

After the terms of the initial members have expired, the terms of all members, except the appointed member of the governing body, shall expire four years from the expiration date of the terms of their predecessors.

The reorganized authority shall consist of newly appointed board members numbering not less than five nor more than eleven (11) members appointed initially by the Mayor and subsequently by the governing body.
The city originally nominated this district to the National Register of Historic Places in 1980; it is the oldest residential neighborhood listed on the National Register in Cheyenne. 2.
The four parcels adjacent to this right-of-way were unbuildable parcels in the original Waterford Square plat and they continue to be so with this plat.
All agreements, ownership, and restrictions associated with Lots 28 and 29, Block 7, and Lots 1 and 31, Block 5 Waterford Square will be continued to all lots associated with this plat.

Section 15-9-134, the mayor, by and with the consent and advice of the local governing body, shall appoint a board of five (5) commissioners of the urban renewal agency selected on the basis of their interest in and knowledge of community planning, urban renewal, and business management.

Any person may be appointed as commissioner if he or she resides within the area of operation of the agency (which shall have the same bounds or limits as the area of operation of the municipality) and is otherwise eligible for appointment under this chapter.

The original appointment of commissioners shall be as follows: one (1) for a term of one (1) year; one (1) for a term of two (2) years; one (1) for a term of three (3) years; one (1) for a term of four (4) years; and one (1) for a term of five (5) years.
Each commissioner shall hold office until his or her successor is appointed and qualified.

A certificate of the appointment or reappointment of any commissioner shall be filed with the clerk of the municipality and the certificate is conclusive evidence of the commissioner’s due and proper appointment.
Each officer shall hold office for a term of one (1) year and until his successor is elected and qualified.

actions.quote: Your territory sales representative will continue to provide support and updates on each of your individual projects.
We will continue to monitor the market and reevaluate our price points based on the best available information.
The supply of resin has continued to decline forcing allocations, delayed shipments or cancellations.
Propex will continue to utilize our market leading production and sourcing capabilities in an effort to support all our customers.

Propex is continuing to aggressively address our strong production and superior sourcing capabilities in an effort to support all our customers; however, the cost pressures of resin availability in conjunction with product available to ship will continue to be longer term in nature.
As we have worked through this difficult situation over the past months, SKAPS has endeavored to continue to supply products to our customers in as timely a manner as possible.
SKAPS will work diligently to continue to provide you with the highest quality products, at competitive prices, in as timely a manner as possible.
We will also diligently monitor the market conditions and continue to communicate with you as we work through this difficult situation.
Rest assured, we are making evety effort to return back to normal production as quickly as possible, and we will continue to keep you updated on our continued site assessments and restart efforts.
“Market conditions continue to remain highly volatile, with resin availability and pricing changing daily,” says Chuck.

In the past, distributors have been able to hold pricing during the longer cycle as the resin price has been less volatile.” GMA and Geosynthetics magazine will continue to monitor this issue and will provide future information to address the wider concerns of the GMA membership.
All other provisions of the original Professional Services Agreement remain unchanged and continue to have full force and effect for the term of the Professional Services Agreement. 7.
If any portion of this Lease shall be held to be invalid or unenforceable for any reason, the remaining provisions shall continue to be valid and enforceable.

actions.quote: Funding priorities will continue to be used to support the low-income residents of Cheyenne. 2.

The City's past programs have focused on community needs that continue to exist including ageing housing, public facility rehabilitation, neighborhood improvements, and social service support for low- income residents.
The City will continue to discuss the affordable housing concept with local developers.
Homeless families with children in Laramie County continue to be a disturbing reality.
This is an area where Cheyenne will continue to provide funding.

The MPO, Building, Development, and Planning offices will continue to work with and encourage developers to build more affordable housing along with encouraging a broader diversity of housing types that can better match housing products to area incomes.
Additional discussions relating to density and strategies to mitigate the adverse effects of density will continue to be an ongoing topic of discussion in the City of Cheyenne.
To calm these reasonable concerns, the City should continue to provide a balanced approach to development in which these issues are addressed in code and are mitigated by our standards.
With adequate assurances in place, elected officials can assure concerned neighbors that their issues will be addressed in a predictable and sufficient manner.
This enables elected officials to approve development projects with greater certainty that they are not neglecting the concerns of area residents they represent.

Annual Action Plan 2021 40 OMB Control No: 2506-0117 (exp. 09/30/2021) AP-85 Other Actions – 91.220(k) Introduction: The Housing & Community Development (H&CD) Office will continue to develop programs and initiatives, designed to improve existing programs, and identify additional sources to better…

The City and its staff will continue to support these agencies and organizations as they serve the community's populations who are most in need of assistance, including the homeless and special needs populations.

The City and its staff will continue to support these agencies and organizations as they serve the community's populations who are most in need of assistance, including the homeless and special needs populations.

The greatest obstacle facing all agencies and organizations who work to meet the underserved needs in the community has been and is expected to continue to be the lack of available funding for meeting the level of need that exists in the community.

Actions planned to foster and maintain affordable housing The H&CD Office will continue to work with the City Planning and Development Department and MPO Office to support PlanCheyenne and will offer support to other agencies that work with and foster affordable housing.

The H&CD Office will continue to provide funding for homeowner rehabilitation projects in an effort to maintain the local affordable housing stock and provide funding for s80grantees who have affordable housing projects.

actions.quote: Funding priorities will continue to be used to support the low-income residents of Cheyenne. 2.

The City's past programs have focused on community needs that continue to exist including ageing housing, public facility rehabilitation, neighborhood improvements, and social service support for low- income residents.
The City will continue to discuss the affordable housing concept with local developers.
Homeless families with children in Laramie County continue to be a disturbing reality.
This is an area where Cheyenne will continue to provide funding.

The MPO, Building, Development, and Planning offices will continue to work with and encourage developers to build more affordable housing along with encouraging a broader diversity of housing types that can better match housing products to area incomes.
Additional discussions relating to density and strategies to mitigate the adverse effects of density will continue to be an ongoing topic of discussion in the City of Cheyenne.
To calm these reasonable concerns, the City should continue to provide a balanced approach to development in which these issues are addressed in code and are mitigated by our standards.
With adequate assurances in place, elected officials can assure concerned neighbors that their issues will be addressed in a predictable and sufficient manner.
This enables elected officials to approve development projects with greater certainty that they are not neglecting the concerns of area residents they represent.

Annual Action Plan 2021 40 OMB Control No: 2506-0117 (exp. 09/30/2021) AP-85 Other Actions – 91.220(k) Introduction: The Housing & Community Development (H&CD) Office will continue to develop programs and initiatives, designed to improve existing programs, and identify additional sources to better…

The City and its staff will continue to support these agencies and organizations as they serve the community's populations who are most in need of assistance, including the homeless and special needs populations.

The City and its staff will continue to support these agencies and organizations as they serve the community's populations who are most in need of assistance, including the homeless and special needs populations.

The greatest obstacle facing all agencies and organizations who work to meet the underserved needs in the community has been and is expected to continue to be the lack of available funding for meeting the level of need that exists in the community.

Actions planned to foster and maintain affordable housing The H&CD Office will continue to work with the City Planning and Development Department and MPO Office to support PlanCheyenne and will offer support to other agencies that work with and foster affordable housing.

The H&CD Office will continue to provide funding for homeowner rehabilitation projects in an effort to maintain the local affordable housing stock and provide funding for s80grantees who have affordable housing projects.

City Staff is directed to prepare a priority list of any related or remaining capital construction or operation and maintenance requests for the August 21, 2012 voter- approved projects to be funded by the excess tax funds in Fiscal Year 2020 or beyond.

actions.quote: The City's past programs have focased on community needs that continue to exist including aging housing and infrastructure, neighborhood improvements, and social service supports for low-income residents.

Cheyenne believes the programs proposed for the 2018 Action Plan year and goals for the five-year planning period, are like those used in the past, and continue to be the most efficient and effective use of Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) funds.
The Governor of Wyoming has appointed a homeless coordinator.
The City will continue to discuss the affordable housing concept with local developers.
This is an area where Cheyenne will continue to provide funding.

The MPO, Planning, Development and Building offices will continue to work with and encourage developers to build more affordable housing along with encouraging a broader diversity of housing types that can better match housing products to area incomes.
Additional discussions relating to density and strategies to mitigate the adverse effects of density will continue to be an ongoing topic of discussion in the City of Cheyenne.
To calm these reasonable concerns, the City should continue to provide a balanced approach to development in which these issues are addressed in code and are mitigated by our standards.
With adequate assurances in place, elected officials can assure concerned neighbors that their issues will be addressed in a predictable and sufficient manner.
This enables elected officials to approve development projects with greater certainty that they are not neglecting the concerns of area residents they represent.

Annual Action Plan 2018 43 OMB Control No: 2506-0117 (exp. 06/30/2018) AP-85 Other Actions – 91.220(k) Introduction: The Housing & Community Development (H&CD) Office will continue to develop programs and initiatives, designed to improve existing programs, and identify additional sources to better…

The city and its staff will continue to support these agencies and organizations as they serve the community's populations who are most in need of assistance, including the homeless and special needs populations.

The city and its staff will continue to support these agencies and organizations as they serve the community's populations who are most in need of assistance, including the homeless and special needs populations.

The greatest obstacle facing all agencies and organizations who work to meet the underserved needs in the community has been and is expected to continue to be the lack of available funding for meeting the level of need that exists in the community.

Actions planned to foster and maintain affordable housing The H&CD Office will continue to work with the City Planning offices to support PlanCheyenne and will offer support to other agencies that work with and foster affordable housing.

The H&CD Office will also continue to provide funding for homeowner rehabilitation projects in an effort to maintain the local affordable housing stock and also continue to provide funding for first time homebuyers to assist with down payment and closing costs.

That Section 2.08.010, Appointment and term – Removal – Vacancy, of Chapter 2.08, City Officers and Employees Generally, of Title 2, Administration and Personnel, of the code of the City of Cheyenne is hereby amended as forth in this ordinance to provide for the appointment of the director of the d…
Each appointed officer APPOINTED PURSUANT TO SUB-SECTION 2.28.010 A., shall hold office for A the term of two (2) years or until his or her successor is appointed and qualified.

Each officer appointed pursuant to Sub-Section 2.08.010 A., shall hold office for a term of two (2) years, PROVIDED HOWEVER, THAT THE SPECIFIC BEGINNING AND ENDING DATES OF THE TERM OF APPOINTMENT SHALL BE SPECIFIED IN THE CERTIFICATE OF APPOINTMENT.
This can be seen with the Police Department’s comments relating to additional officers needed to continue to provide the same level of service.

The Council shall consist of not more than seven (7) members appointed by the Mayor, subject to the approval of the City Council, to serve without compensation, except that members of the Council may be reimbursed for approved expenses incurred in the performance of official duties.
Each member of the Council shall serve for a term of two (2) years, except that three (3) of the initial members appointed to the Council shall serve one (1) year terms.

actions.quote: Our community members continue to show what it means to ‘do our part’ in contributing to parks, trails, open space, and recreation programs, as demonstrated by the input they provided to crafting this plan.
Our recreation services continue to adapt and change to meet community needs.
There is an opportunity to continue to enhance open space surrounding trails to improve experiences, healthy natural systems and wildlife habitat, and create a more resilient community.
These dynamics require thoughtful, inclusive planning to ensure parks and recreation continue to serve all residents effectively.

As global challenges like climate change continue to impact local environments, parks will need to be adapted to mitigate these risks through resilient infrastructure, enhanced green spaces, and innovative design solutions that prioritize public and natural systems health.

BARRIERS » 60% of respondents identified seasonal weather constraints as the most common reason preventing the use of parks and recreation facilities. » 22% of respondents selected that facilities are often booked or overcrowded.
With the addition and expansion of the trail system, additional staff will be required.
The City should continue to monitor the programs, activities and use of the facilities, and make adjustments accordingly.
The City should continue to adjust facilities according to user trends and demands.
PLAN FRAMEWORK INTRODUCTION This chapter provides guidance and recommendations for the City of Cheyenne to continue to provide high quality parks and programs into the future.

UNION REPRESENTATION In the event any Member of the Department appears before the Deputy Fire Chief, Fire Chief, the Mayor or their designee, for work-related disciplinary action, that Member shall have the option of having one elected Union representative present.
The elected Union representative shall be granted time off without loss of wages.
The Member will continue to receive all specialty, education, longevity, acting and other pays the Member is entitled to for the duration of the assignment. 46 SECTION 24.

Members will continue to accrue benefits during the usage of sick leave from the Department Sick Leave Bank.
A set selection of items for new recruits will be agreed upon between the Fire Chief and the Union, or its designee.

actions.quote: Funding priorities will continue to support the low- income residents of Cheyenne. 2.

The City's past programs have focused on community needs that continue to exist including ageing housing, public facility rehabilitation, neighborhood improvements, and social service support for low- income residents.
At this meeting, H & CD staff will provide a staff report.
The City will continue to discuss the affordable housing concept with local developers.
Homeless families with children in Laramie County continue to be a disturbing reality.
This is an area where Cheyenne will continue to provide funding.

The Planning and Development offices and Compliance Division will continue to work with and encourage developers to build more affordable housing that creates a broader diversity of housing types to better match housing products with area incomes.
Additional discussions relating to density and strategies to mitigate its effects will continue to be an ongoing topic of discussion in the City of Cheyenne.
To calm these reasonable concerns, the City should continue to provide a balanced approach to development in which these issues are addressed in code and are mitigated by our standards.
With adequate assurances in place, elected officials can reassure concerned neighbors that their issues will be addressed in a predictable and sufficient manner.
This enables elected officials to approve development projects with greater certainty that they are not neglecting the concerns of their constituents.

actions.quote: The division remains dedicated to fostering safe, stable, and affordable housing solutions as we continue to identify and implement strategies that enhance our community's well-being.
Under the Public Service Category, projects like the Safehouse Client Emergency Expenses and Utility Assistance programs have been selected due to the increasing demand for such services in Cheyenne.

The Equal Justice Wyoming Foundation's Civil Legal Services for Low-Income Individuals in Cheyenne is another vital project selected for its potential to address the significant gap in legal aid for those living below 200% of the federal poverty level.

The Annual Action Plan goals align with those included in the 5-Year Plan. • Conversion of Public Housing: CHA plans to convert Public Housing to Project-Based Rental Assistance or Project-based Vouchers under the Rental Assistance Demonstration (RAD) program. • Capital Fund Utilization: CHA will c…
The Board consists of five members, two members appointed by the City of Cheyenne, two members appointed by Laramie County, and one member appointed by the City and County in alternating terms.
If the DDA Board desires more discussion on this item, this can be postponed to a special meeting next week.

Even as we work to meld with the other Univerus solutions into our Unity Suite we still function autonomously as Univerus Routing, and continue to work with clients as an independent solution, now with the backing and support of a larger corporation.
City of Cheyenne staff will walk the trail centerline with the Contractor for final approval of field design prior to construction.

actions.quote: As a representative of government (elected or employed) or as a member of emergency services, it is imperative you know the content of the plan.
Laramie County and its cities and towns will continue to be exposed to the hazards identified in this plan as well as others which may develop in the future. 2.
Local government officials, both elected and appointed, will, to the best of their abilities carry out all responsibilities regarding public safety and the protection of property.

Roles and Responsibilities A mayor, city representative, county commissioner or elected official, as a jurisdiction’s Chief Elected Official (CEO), is responsible for the public safety and welfare of the people of that jurisdiction.
Direction and Control The final responsibility for all emergency management belongs to the Laramie County Commissioners and the elected officials of the jurisdiction(s) affected by the emergency.

Support positions for the elected officials are:  Cheyenne/Laramie County Emergency Manager  City/County Attorneys  Public Information Officer  City/County Risk Managers  City/County Clerks  Human Resources Manager  City/County Treasurers Continuity of Government Operations Each agency is re…
This activation level requires the acquisition and/or use of special resources and will require support from selected departments.
An Emergency Support Function (ESF) leader will be appointed for each ESF needed during an event.
During an emergency the PIO serves as the spokesman for the elected official(s) in charge of the emergency.
In the absence of a PIO the elected official(s) for the affected jurisdiction(s) should serve as the point of contact for media.
FEMA established the community lifelines during 2018 to address this need and has continued to improve and refine its implementation based on lessons learned.
ESF #1 will continue to assess transportation infrastructure and make recommendations of restoration to the EOC and local officials. 2.
The coordinator will continue to direct support agencies in transportation needs. 3.

ESF #2 will continue to coordinate local actions to provide for the restoration of the telecommunications interface between local agencies, local and state governments, and with outside organizations.
The coordinator will continue to direct support agencies in communication needs.
Provide emergency repair of damaged infrastructure and critical facilities in coordination with elected officials and department heads. 2.
Resource requests will be directed through the EOC and the elected official(s) with the affected jurisdiction.
The ESF #3 coordinator will continue to provide support during the recovery phase of disaster operations. 2.
Support agencies will continue to provide assistance as needed to the ESF #3 coordinator as requested. 3.
The ESF #5 Coordinator is a member of the Chief Elected Official(s) staff and will: a.
ESF #6 will continue to assess and coordinate required resources through the transition from the Response to Recovery phase. 2.
The coordinator will continue to direct support agencies in transportation needs.
Coordinate with local elected officials and legal services to contract, review and approve disaster response and recovery logistical support. 5.
Advise Chief Elected Officials on priorities for energy restoration, assistance and supply.
The authority to order an evacuation lies with local government or the governor, with the elected chief executive officers in Laramie County holding the formal authority.

If requests from the FBI are for state law enforcement assistance and non-law enforcement assistance, a local or state liaison officer will be appointed and the request forwarded to the Wyoming Office of Homeland Security. i.

The Chief Elected Officials will, as soon as practical, request assistance from the State of Wyoming based on the escalation of the situation, and in coordination with the Cheyenne/Laramie County Emergency Management Agency and the investigating jurisdiction.

All jurisdictions should, therefore, be aware that EMA will continue to assist them in obtaining the necessary resources to mitigate emergency and disaster events when situations exceed their local capabilities.
The role of Emergency Management will continue to be one of coordination and will not replace the authority or responsibility of local officials to exercise control over emergency or disaster events.
The PIO staff will disseminate Special News Advisories and other emergency public information materials to the media directly using its contact list.

"Public official" or "public member" means any elected or appointed Cheyenne City Council person and any appointed board or commission member serving on a board or commission of the City of Cheyenne.

"Public member" means a member of the public not employed by the city and who is not a "public official," who is appointed to a board or commission while acting within "official responsibility" or "official capacity" of the city of Casper.

"Public official" or "public member" means: every elected or appointed Casper City Council person, and every appointed board or commission member serving on a board or commission of the city of Casper.
The Board consists of five members, two members appointed by the City of Cheyenne, two members appointed by Laramie County, and one member appointed by the City and County in alternating terms.
Items marked with * indicate projects that we will continue to collect funds (CFCs and 6th Penny) over several years but will be required to fund through reserves in the current FY.

Board shall mean the Board of Trustees as designated by the Initial Participants to administer and supervise the affairs of the Trust and such new or successor Trustees as shall be appointed as provided in this Agreement.
Maintenance of Records - The Administrator, or such other person appointed by the Board, shall record the allocations of shares in the records of the Trust. 11.3.

The Initial Participants have by this Indenture appointed the following persons as initial trustees (the “Initial Trustees”) with terms ending on the following dates: Mr. Matthew McBurnett - June 30, 2021 Mr. Jonathan Teichert - June 30, 2022 Mr. William Novotny - June 30, 2023 Trustees may succeed…

The appointment of any Trustee (other than an individual who was serving as a Trustee immediately prior to such election) shall not become effective unless and until such person has agreed in writing to serve as a Trustee and to be bound by the terms of this Indenture.

actions.quote: Purpose: This policy is intended to help potential donors understand how the City decides whether to accept a proposed gift and how that donor can be recognized and thanked; to guide decisions of the City, elected officials, and staff.
The staff will work with the donor to select a variety of options to thank and recognize them for their gift.
Often many people may be “behind the scenes contributors” to a major gift (e.g., elected officials, staff members, or community leaders).
Funding priorities will continue to be used to support the low-income residents of Cheyenne. 2.

The City's past programs have focused on community needs that continue to exist including ageing housing, public facility rehabilitation, neighborhood improvements, and social service support for low- income residents.
The City will continue to discuss the affordable housing concept with local developers.
Homeless families with children in Laramie County continue to be a disturbing reality.
This is an area where Cheyenne will continue to provide funding.

The Planning and Development offices and Compliance Division will continue to work with and encourage developers to build more affordable housing that creates a broader diversity of housing types to better match housing products with area incomes.
Additional discussions relating to density and strategies to mitigate its effects will continue to be an ongoing topic of discussion in the City of Cheyenne.
To calm these reasonable concerns, the City should continue to provide a balanced approach to development in which these issues are addressed in code and are mitigated by our standards.
With adequate assurances in place, elected officials can reassure concerned neighbors that their issues will be addressed in a predictable and sufficient manner.
This enables elected officials to approve development projects with greater certainty that they are not neglecting the concerns of their constituents.

CTP will continue to provide complementary paratransit service to eligible users within three-quarters of a mile of the fixed-route system.
Each of the four fixed-routes will operate hourly service and microtransit will continue to cover the areas outside the fixed-route coverage.

New Fleet Needs Under Service Plan The phases of CTP’s service plan, outlined previously, will continue to provide microtransit service within four zones and slowly reimplement fixed-route service, from two to four routes over the next 10 years.

Multiagency taskforce activations may be made when the duly elected Laramie County Sheriff, or his or her designee, and the duly appointed Chief of Police, or his or her designee, agree to the activation. e.

actions.quote: These manholes will continue to be within the floodplain and should be evaluated to limit infiltration during a storm event where water is being detained in this location.
The 5’ diameter culvert was selected as the maximum diameter that can be bored while adhering to UPRR deflection constraints.
The widened sidewalk would then switch to the north side of the road where it would continue until meeting the stubbed sidewalk at the Christensen Road intersection.
The current lane configuration will continue to align with WYDOT’s need for capacity through the intersection.
This means that, as the East Pershing corridor and surrounding area develops further, the peak runoff rate will continue to decrease.
It is proposed that the south side ditch section continue to be used for this purpose, while allowing for a wider sidewalk on the berm on the north side of the Pershing Pointe detention pond.

The south side of the road has historic drainage issues, and the proposed design takes care to not direct any additional runoff flows into this area. 34 - East Pershing Boulevard Plan PUBLIC ENGAGEMENT The second public engagement meeting was held at Baggs Elementary School on March 24th from 5:30…
